$comment: What to say when nothing was listening. Both clients drop a numeric no handler claimed, which is right for the hundreds of replies that carry data and wrong for the refusals: a refusal is the server's answer to something the user just did, so dropping it means they watch nothing happen and are never told why. Shared by tests/shared/numerics.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest.
$unclaimed: Given a numeric and its parameters, the text to show — or null to stay quiet. Our own nick is the first parameter and is dropped; the rest is what the refusal was about.

unclaimed.name: a channel that is not there
the server password was wrong, and the connection is about to close
banned from the server, which otherwise looks like the network being down
params: You are banned from this server: spam
unclaimed.message: You are banned from this server: spam

unclaimed.name: forwarded somewhere else, so the room you land in is not the one you asked for
not an operator
params: Permission Denied- You're not an IRC operator
unclaimed.message: Permission Denied- You're not an IRC operator

unclaimed.name: a private message that went nowhere, because the other end blocks strangers
and the follow-up saying they were told you tried
params: has been informed that you messaged them
unclaimed.message: bob has been informed that you messaged them

unclaimed.name: somebody tried to message you while you were the one refusing
params: is messaging you, and you have umode +g.
unclaimed.message: carol carol@example.org is messaging you, and you have umode +g.

unclaimed.name: a mode letter this server does not have
a lone parameter is read as the sentence, because that is what servers send

$quiet: Numerics that are dropped. The ordinary replies carry data rather than news, and a client that printed them would be answering its own questions out loud; a numeric with nothing to read is not worth a line either.

monitor, which has handlers of its own either side of this range
four digits is not a numeric
nor when the description is only spaces
